q: Which Article of the Constitution declares that the laws in force at the commencement of the Constitution shall continue in force?
explanation: Article 372 provided for the continuance of the laws in force at the commencement of the Constitution and it was repealed by the 24th Amendment.

q: Constituent Assembly took:
options: 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to complete the Constitution
explanation: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to complete the Constitution and it held 11 sessions over 165 days.

q: Which schedule of the Constitution contains the list of the recognised languages?
explanation: The Second Schedule lists the 24 languages recognised by the Constitution, with Hindi and English as the official languages of the Union under Article 343.

q: The 'Eighth Schedule' now contains how many languages?
explanation: The Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages and it now has 22 after the additions of Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali by the 92nd Amendment.

q: The 'Seventh Schedule' of the Constitution contains how many subjects in the Concurrent List?
explanation: The Concurrent List has 52 subjects, the Union List has 100 and the State List has 61.

q: Sovereignty of India is:
options: divided between the Union and the states
explanation: The sovereignty of India is not vested in any single authority and it is divided between the Union and the states as the Constitution provides.

q: The 'Citizenship Act, 1955' provides for the acquisition of the citizenship by:
explanation: The Citizenship Act of 1955 provides for the acquisition of the citizenship by the registration and the naturalisation and it also deals with the deprivation and the renunciation.

q: The 'Citizenship (Amendment) Act of 2023' provides for:
options: The change of the citizenship to the dual
The removal of the condition of the three years of residence and the waiver of the deprivation for the persons born in India
The introduction of the fast track citizenship
explanation: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act of 2023 removed the condition of the three years of residence for the naturalisation and the waiver of the deprivation for those born in India.

q: The 'Article 15(3)' enables the state to make special provisions for:
explanation: Article 15(3) enables the state to make the special provisions for the women and the children and Article 15(4) for the socially and the educationally backward classes.

q: The 'Article 15(5)' was inserted by the:
explanation: The 93rd Amendment of 2005 inserted Article 15(5) to provide for the admission of the socially and the educationally backward classes, including the SC and the ST, in the private educational institutions.

q: The 'Article 16(4A)' provides for:
options: The extension of the reservation to the private sector
The reservation of the promotions for the SC and the ST in the services
explanation: Article 16(4A), inserted by the 77th Amendment of 1995, provides for the reservation of the promotions for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in the services.

q: The 'Article 16(6)' was inserted by the:
explanation: Article 16(6), inserted by the 103rd Amendment of 2019, provides for the reservation of the seats for the economically weaker sections in the services.

q: The freedom of trade and the profession is:
options: subject to the public interest and the reasonable restrictions
explanation: Article 19(1)(g) guarantees the freedom of the profession but it is subject to the reasonable restrictions in the public interest, as the Supreme Court held in the M.P. Association of Dealers case of 2021.

q: The right to privacy and the right to a clean environment and the right to livelihood are:
explanation: The Supreme Court has read the right to privacy, the right to a clean environment, the right to livelihood, the right to health and the right to shelter into Article 21.

q: The 'Article 20(2)' provides that:
options: No person shall be arrested without the warrant
No person shall be deprived of his life
No person shall be prevented from the speech
No person shall be tried and convicted for an offence except as provided by the law
explanation: Article 20(2) provides that no person shall be tried and convicted of any offence except in accordance with the procedure established by law, and the narrower interpretation of the double jeopardy was given in the Sajjan Singh case.

q: The 'Article 22(1)' requires that:
options: No person arrested shall be denied the right to be informed of the grounds of the arrest
The arrest must be with a warrant
The arrested must be produced within 48 hours
The arrested must be given a lawyer
explanation: Article 22(1) provides that no person who is arrested shall be denied the right to be informed of the grounds of the arrest and Article 22(2) provides the right to be produced before the magistrate within 24 hours.

q: The 'Article 25(1)' guarantees the freedom of religion and it is subject to:
options: Public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III
explanation: Article 25(1) guarantees the freedom of conscience and the religion but it is subject to the public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Article 30(1) is correct?
options: Only the linguistic minorities have this right
It applies only to the government institutions
All the minorities, whether religious or linguistic, have the right to establish and administer the educational institutions of their choice
Only the religious minorities have this right
explanation: Article 30(1) guarantees to all the minorities, whether religious or linguistic, the right to establish and administer the educational institutions of their choice.

q: The right under Article 32 cannot be suspended except as provided:
options: by Article 359 during a national emergency
explanation: Article 32, the heart and soul of the Constitution, cannot be suspended except as provided by Article 359 during a national emergency.

q: The 'Article 39A' was inserted by the 42nd Amendment and it directs the state to secure:
options: The promotion of the cottage industries
The equal justice and the free legal aid
explanation: Article 39A directs the state to secure that the legal system promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity and to provide free legal aid to the citizens.

q: The 'Article 38(1)' directs the state to promote the welfare of the individual by securing and protecting:
options: A social order in which justice, social, economic and political justice shall inform all the national institutions
The development of the heavy industries
explanation: Article 38(1) directs the state to promote the welfare of the individual by securing and protecting a social order in which the justice, the social, the economic and the political justice shall inform all the national institutions.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Article 40 is correct?
options: It directs the organisation of the village panchayats
It directs the separation of the judiciary
It directs the promotion of the cottage industries
It directs the protection of the monuments
explanation: Article 40 directs the state to organise the village panchayats and to endow them with the powers to enable them to function as the units of the self-government.

q: The 'Article 45' was amended by the 86th Amendment and it now provides for:
options: The free education till the age of fourteen
The promotion of the cottage industries
The early childhood care and education of the children below six years
explanation: The 86th Amendment of 2002 replaced the provision of the free and compulsory education of the children of the age of six to fourteen with the early childhood care and education below the age of six.

q: The 'Article 47' was amended in 1976 to include:
options: The raising of the level of nutrition and the improvement of the standard of living and the public health
The promotion of the scientific research
explanation: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 amended Article 47 to add the raising of the level of nutrition and the improvement of the standard of living and the public health.

q: The 'Article 49' of the Constitution:
options: Deals with the organisation of the panchayats
Deals with the promotion of the peace
Directs the state to protect the monuments and the places of national importance
Deals with the separation of the judiciary
explanation: Article 49 places on the state the duty to protect the monuments and the places of national importance and it was added by the 42nd Amendment.

q: The 'Article 51A(g)' of the Constitution:
options: Requires the citizen to protect the natural environment and to have compassion for the living creatures
Requires the citizen to pay the taxes
Requires the citizen to serve the defence
explanation: The duty to protect and improve the natural environment, to have compassion for the living creatures, to develop the scientific temper and to safeguard the public property is in Article 51A.

q: The 'Article 51A(e)' provides that:
options: Every citizen shall serve the armed forces
Every citizen shall protect the cows
Every citizen shall be educated in the manner in which the State shall determine
Every citizen shall pay the taxes
explanation: The 86th Amendment added Article 51A(k) to the list of the fundamental duties, with the education of the child between six and fourteen years as a duty of the parent.

q: The 'fundamental duties' are not enforceable by the courts:
options: They are enforceable in the High Courts
They are enforceable in the Supreme Court
explanation: The fundamental duties are not enforceable by the courts and they are, in the words of the Savarkar Committee, a 'summary of those social and political obligations which the Constitution expects the citizens to perform'.

q: The 'Article 246A' gives the concurrent power of the Parliament and the state legislature in the field of:
explanation: Article 246A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, gives the concurrent power of the Parliament and the state legislatures in the field of education.

q: The 'Article 263' provides for the Inter-State Council, which was set up in:
explanation: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 by an executive resolution of the Union government, though Article 263 provides for its establishment by the President.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Article 280?
options: The Finance Commission is appointed every fifth year by the President
It is elected by the Parliament
It is chaired by the Prime Minister
explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier if necessary and it is chaired by a person appointed by the President.

q: The 'GST Council' decisions require:
options: A simple majority of the states
A three-fourths majority of the weighted votes of the states and a simple majority of the central government
explanation: The GST Council is a joint forum of the Union and the states and the decisions need a three-fourths majority of the weighted votes of the states and a simple majority of the central government.

q: The Union List has:
options: 100 subjects and the State List has 61 and the Concurrent List has 52
explanation: The Seventh Schedule has the three lists: the Union List of 100 subjects, the State List of 61 subjects and the Concurrent List of 52 subjects.

q: The 'Money Bill' is defined in Article:
explanation: Article 110 of the Constitution defines a money bill and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha certifies the bills under it.

q: A bill which provides:
options: A bill of the private member
A bill which provides for the taxation and the borrowing and the appropriation of the money
explanation: A financial bill is a bill which provides for the taxation, the borrowing or the appropriation of the money and the Financial Bill is a subset of the money bill.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The President is correct?
explanation: The Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha submit their resignations to the President, while the Speaker of the Rajya Sabha submits his to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

q: no-confidence motion can be:
options: moved only in the Lok Sabha
explanation: A no-confidence motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha, where the government holds the collective responsibility, and it requires a simple majority of the members present and voting.

q: Censure motion can be:
options: moved against a minister and it can be moved in the Rajya Sabha
explanation: A censure motion can be moved against a minister and it can be moved in either house, though in practice it is moved only in the Lok Sabha, and the Speaker's decision is final.

q: The Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are:
explanation: Article 100 provides for the election of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker by the members of the Lok Sabha from amongst themselves.

q: The 'Article 122' deals with:
options: The vacancies of the seats of the members of the Parliament
explanation: Article 122 provides for the vacancies of the seats of the members of the Parliament and the procedure of the by-election in the case of the pre-election vacancy.

q: The 'Article 123' provides for the ordinance and every ordinance must be laid before the Parliament within:
explanation: Every ordinance must be laid before the Parliament and it ceases to operate six weeks after the Parliament reassembles, unless it is approved by the houses.

q: The 'Public Accounts Committee' is chaired by:
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Committee of Estimates
explanation: The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha, and it is chaired by the Chairman of the Committee of Estimates.

q: The 'Estimates Committee' has:
options: Thirty members, all from the Lok Sabha
explanation: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all elected from the Lok Sabha, and it is the largest of the financial committees.

q: The 'Supreme Court' has the power to do all except:
options: To transfer the cases from the High Court to itself
To create a new High Court
To take the suo motu notice of the matters of the public importance
To transfer the cases from one High Court to another
explanation: The Supreme Court can take the suo motu notice, transfer the cases between the High Courts and transfer the cases to itself, but it cannot create a new High Court.

q: It enables the Supreme Court to pass such orders as are:
options: for the review of the judgments
for the transfer of the judges
the Supreme Court the power to make the laws
explanation: Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass such decree or order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.

q: The 'Article 137' provides for:
options: The appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in the criminal cases
explanation: Article 137 provides for the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in the criminal cases and Article 134 in the civil cases.

q: The 'High Court' can be moved for the enforcement of the fundamental rights under Article:
explanation: The High Courts can be moved for the enforcement of the fundamental rights under Article 226, which is wider in scope than Article 32 of the Supreme Court.

q: The opinion of the Supreme Court on a presidential reference is:
explanation: The opinion of the Supreme Court on a reference under Article 143 is not binding but is of great value and the authority and the Parliament and the executive are bound to take it into consideration.

q: The 'High Court judges' are appointed by:
options: The Governor in consultation with the CJI, the Chief Justice and the state Chief Justice
explanation: The High Court judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the CJI, the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Governor, and they hold office until the age of 62.

q: The 'Judicial review' of the Indian Constitution was first asserted in:
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
explanation: In the Shankari Prasad case of 1951 the Supreme Court asserted the power of the judicial review over the constitutional amendments, reversing the A.K. Gopalan decision of 1950.

q: The 'basic structure' doctrine was propounded in the:
explanation: The Kesavananda Bharati case of 1973, by a 7-6 majority, laid down the basic structure doctrine and it was reaffirmed in the Minerva Mills case of 1980.

q: The 'Doctrine of Eclipse' was propounded in:
explanation: In the Golaknath case of 1967 the Supreme Court held that an unconstitutional law is dormant but not dead, and the Kesavananda Bharati case of 1973 modified it with the basic structure doctrine.

q: The 'K.S. Puttaswamy' case of 2017 held that the right to privacy:
options: Is not a right in India
Can be restricted by the executive
Is a fundamental right under Article 21
explanation: In the K.S. Puttaswamy case of 2017 a nine-judge bench of the Supreme Court unanimously held that the right to privacy is a fundamental right protected under Article 21.

q: The 'S.R. Bommai' case of 1994 held that:
options: The proclamation of the President's Rule is subject to the judicial review and the federalism is a basic feature
The President's Rule is beyond the judicial review
The Parliament may amend the basic structure
explanation: In the S.R. Bommai case of 1994 the Supreme Court held that the proclamation of the President's Rule under Article 356 is subject to the judicial review and it laid down the guidelines for the floor test.

q: The 'Article 124' provides that the removal of a Supreme Court judge requires a resolution in each house of Parliament:
options: Passed by a two-thirds majority of the total membership of that house and by a majority of the total membership of the house
explanation: The removal of a Supreme Court judge under Article 124(4) requires a resolution passed in each house of Parliament by a two-thirds majority of the total membership of that house and by a majority of the total membership of the house.

q: It is a court of record and the law declared:
options: by it is binding on all the courts in India
explanation: The Supreme Court is a court of record and the law declared by it is binding on all the courts in India and it is the final court of appeal.

q: The district judges are:
options: appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court
explanation: Article 233 provides for the appointment of the district judges by the Governor in consultation with the High Court and Article 235 gives the control of the subordinate courts to the High Court.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Article 136?
options: The President may transfer the cases
The tribunals may transfer the cases
The Supreme Court may grant the special leave to appeal from any court or tribunal in India
The High Courts may transfer the cases to the Supreme Court
explanation: Article 136 empowers the Supreme Court to grant the special leave to appeal from any judgment, determination, sentence or order passed by any court or tribunal in India.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Article 124?
options: The judges of the Supreme Court hold office until the age of 65 years
For a fixed term of 12 years
explanation: The Supreme Court judges hold office until the age of 65 and the High Court judges until the age of 62, and the retirement age was raised by the 15th Amendment of 1963.

q: The 'Article 324' provides that the Election Commissioner can be removed by:
options: The President on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner
explanation: Before the 2023 law the Election Commissioners could be removed only on the CEC's recommendation, and the 2023 amendment gave the CEC the status of a Supreme Court judge.

q: The 'NOTA' was made mandatory to be counted from:
explanation: The Election Commission made the counting of the NOTA votes mandatory with its order of 2022, although the number of the NOTA votes is still not published in the results.

q: The 'Delimitation Commission' is chaired by:
explanation: The Delimitation Commission, set up under Article 82, is chaired by a retired Supreme Court judge with two members of the Indian Civil Services and its orders have the force of law.

q: The 'Electoral Bonds' were introduced in India in:
explanation: The electoral bonds, issued by the State Bank of India, were introduced in 2018 and the Supreme Court struck them down in February 2024.

q: The 'Model Code of Conduct' came into force with:
options: The Model Code of Conduct of 1974
The Model Code of Conduct of 1951
The Model Code of Conduct of 1985
The Model Code of Conduct of 1968
explanation: The Model Code of Conduct was evolved in 1968 and it is enforced by the Election Commission, and the violations are not punishable in the courts.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The accounts of the Union is correct?
options: The accounts of the Union, the states and the bodies financed substantially by the public revenues
explanation: The CAG audits the accounts of the Union and of the states and of the bodies and the authorities that are substantially financed from the public revenues.

q: The 'CAG' is:
options: An executive body under the Ministry of Finance
explanation: The CAG is a constitutional body under Article 148 and the CAG (DPC) Act of 1971 gave it the statutory status and the powers of the civil court.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the UPSC is correct?
options: It is a constitutional body under Article 315
explanation: The UPSC is a constitutional body under Article 315 and it advises the President and the state governments on the recruitment and the service matters.

q: State Public Service Commission is:
explanation: The State Public Service Commissions are the constitutional bodies under Article 315 and they were made the constitutional bodies by the 42nd Amendment of 1976.

q: The 'Election Commission' became a multi-member body on the recommendation of:
explanation: The Dinesh Goswami Committee of 1975 recommended the multi-member Election Commission and the CEC and the ECs were given the statutory status in 1993.

q: The 'Lokpal and Lokayuktas' have their statutory basis in:
explanation: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act of 2013 gave the statutory basis to the two ombudsmen, and the first Lokpal chairperson was Justice P. C. Ghose.

q: The 'NHRC' was constituted under the:
explanation: The National Human Rights Commission is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act of 1993 and the 2019 amendment brought the state commissions also under the Act.

q: The 'CIC' was constituted under:
explanation: The Central Information Commission is a statutory body under the RTI Act of 2005 and it hears the appeals of the citizens who are denied the information by the public authorities.

q: The 'NCBC' was given the statutory status in:
explanation: The National Commission for Backward Classes was given the statutory status by the NCBC Act of 1993 and it has the powers of the civil court.

q: The 'National Commission for Women' was set up in:
explanation: The National Commission for Women was set up in 1990 under the NCW Act of 1990 following the recommendations of the Committee on the Status of Women in India.

q: In the context of the Article 324, which of the following is correct?
options: The CEC has a fixed term of five years
The CEC is appointed for life
The CEC can be removed only like a judge of the Supreme Court after the 2023 amendment
The CEC can be removed at will by the President
explanation: After the 2023 amendment the CEC holds office for six years or up to the age of 65 and can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, and the other commissioners are removed on his recommendation.

q: The '40th Amendment' of 1976:
options: Made the President's election to the two houses and the state legislatures and the emergency provisions beyond judicial review
It gave the President the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha
explanation: The 40th and the 42nd Amendments of 1976 made the President's election and the emergency provisions beyond the judicial review and the 43rd and the 44th Amendments of 1977-78 partly reversed them.

q: The '44th Amendment' of 1978:
options: Restricted the emergency and the ordinance and restored the five-year term of the Lok Sabha
It gave the President the ordinance power
explanation: The 44th Amendment of 1978 restricted the emergency and the ordinance, made the emergency approval by the Parliament mandatory within a month and restored the five-year term of the Lok Sabha.

q: The '52nd Amendment' of 1985:
options: Added the Tenth Schedule with the anti-defection provisions
explanation: The 52nd Amendment of 1985 added the Tenth Schedule with the anti-defection provisions and the Supreme Court upheld it in the Kihoto Hollohan case of 1992.

q: The '61st Amendment' of 1988:
options: Reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years
Gave the vote to the 18-year-olds in the parliamentary elections
explanation: The 61st Amendment of 1988 reduced the voting age for the local body elections to 18 and the 61st and the 62nd Amendments together enabled the same for the parliamentary and the assembly elections.

q: The '73rd and 74th Amendments' of 1992:
options: Gave the constitutional status to the Panchayats and the municipalities
explanation: The 73rd and the 74th Amendment Acts of 1992, which came into force on 24 April 1993, gave the constitutional status to the three-tier Panchayati Raj system and the urban local bodies.

q: The '102nd Amendment' of 2018:
options: It amended the Official Languages Act
Gave the constitutional status to the Central Educational Institutions and the Higher Education Institutions Act and the NJAC Act
explanation: The 102nd Amendment of 2018 gave the constitutional status to the Central Educational Institutions (Regulation) Act and the National Judicial Appointments Commission Act.

q: The '105th Amendment' of 2021:
options: Restored the power of the state legislatures in the Eighth Schedule of the Official Languages Act
explanation: The 105th Amendment of 2021 restored the legislative power of the states in the Eighth Schedule of the Official Languages Act, which the 43rd Amendment had abrogated in 1977.

q: The '106th Amendment' of 2021:
options: It created the Delhi market regulator
Provided for the reservation of one-third of the seats for the women in the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies
It amended the Official Languages Act
explanation: The 106th Amendment of 2021, the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, provided for the reservation of not less than one-third of the seats for the women in the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies.

q: The '1st Amendment' of 1951:
options: Added the Ninth Schedule and the reasonable restrictions on the freedom of trade
explanation: The First Amendment of 1951 added the Ninth Schedule to protect the land reform laws, provided for the reasonable restrictions on the freedom of trade and the first set of the territorial changes.

q: The '7th Amendment' of 1956:
options: Reorganised the states on the linguistic lines and enlarged the Lok Sabha
explanation: The Seventh Amendment of 1956 implemented the linguistic reorganisation and enlarged the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies, which restricted the representation of the Anglo-Indians.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Article 368 is correct?
options: A simple majority of the Parliament is enough
The Supreme Court must approve it
The procedure requires a special majority in each house and the ratification by half the states for the federal provisions
explanation: An amendment requires a special majority in each house and, for the provisions touching the federal structure, the ratification by the legislatures of half the states by a simple majority.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Gram Sabha is correct?
options: It can examine the annual plan and the budget of the Gram Panchayat
It approves the master plan of the district
explanation: The Gram Sabha examines the annual plan and the prepared budget of the Gram Panchayat and it may make the recommendations on the allocation of the funds.

q: The 'reservation of the seats for the women' in the local bodies after the 73rd and 74th Amendments:
options: Is at the discretion of the state
Is not less than one-third of the total seats and of the offices of the chairpersons
explanation: Not less than one-third of the total seats and of the offices of the chairpersons in every Panchayat and municipality are reserved for the women and the seats for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes are reserved in proportion to their population.

q: The 'duration of the term' of the Panchayats and the municipalities after the 73rd and 74th Amendments:
options: Is at the pleasure of the state government
Is five years from the date of the first meeting
explanation: The Panchayats and the municipalities shall continue for five years from the date of the first meeting and they must be dissolved if the fresh elections are not held before the expiry of that period.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The Governor is correct?
explanation: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and he is removed in the manner of the Election Commissioner, and the Article 243K provides for the State Election Commission.

q: The 'Ward Committee' in a municipality consists of:
options: Only the elected councillors of that ward
The elected members of the municipality and of the wards within its jurisdiction
The nominees of the state government
The officials of the district administration
explanation: A Ward Committee consists of one or more elected members of the municipality and the elected members of the wards falling within the jurisdiction of the committee and the 74th Amendment makes it compulsory for every municipality with more than three wards.

q: The MGNREGA provides:
options: the unemployment allowance if the work is not provided within 15 days of the demand
the credit at a concessional rate
explanation: The MGNREGA provides for the unemployment allowance to be paid by the state if the work is not provided within 15 days of the demand and within 30 days of the application.

q: The 'Swachh Bharat Mission' and the 'ODF+':
options: It is a certification of the industrial waste
It is the open defecation in the urban areas
The ODF+ status under the rural component requires the waste management and the liquid waste management
explanation: The rural component of the Swachh Bharat Mission has the ODF+ status, which adds the solid and the liquid waste management and the grey water management to the open defecation free status.

q: The Panchayati Raj was:
options: first launched in 1959 in the Nagaur and the Moradabad districts of the Rajasthan and the Etawah of the Uttar Pradesh
explanation: The Panchayati Raj was first launched on 2 October 1959 in the Nagaur and the Moradabad districts of the Rajasthan and the Etawah district of the Uttar Pradesh and it was formally inaugurated on 15 August 1961.

q: The 'Article 294' of the Constitution:
options: Provides that the agreements with the foreign states are valid
explanation: Article 294 provides that the agreements with the foreign states and the other international agreements of the character of the treaties and the agreements are valid and that the federal government may enter into them.

q: The 'Article 282' of the Constitution:
options: Empowers the Union to enter into the agreements with the international financial institutions
explanation: Article 282 empowers the Union to enter into the agreements with the international organisations and the financial institutions like the IMF and the World Bank and to guarantee the loans.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the G4?
options: The G4 is a military alliance
The G4 comprises the permanent members
The G4 nations are India, Brazil, Germany and Japan and they campaign for the reform of the Security Council
The G4 is a trade bloc
explanation: The G4, with India, Brazil, Germany and Japan, campaigns for a permanent seat and a greater representation in the Security Council and it is supported by the Uniting for Consensus group.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the BRICS?
options: The BRICS was the acronym of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa
It was the Brazil, Russia, Indonesia, China and South Africa
It was the Britain, Russia, India, China and Spain
explanation: The BRICS was the Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa and the term was first used by the Jim O'Neill in 2001 and South Africa joined in 2010.

q: The Panchsheel was:
options: first incorporated in the 1954 Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between Tibet and India
explanation: The Panchsheel was first incorporated in the Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Tibet Region of China and India in 1954 and it was adopted in the Agreement of 1954 with China.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The NAM is correct?
options: The NAM is the largest of the three at the Bandung of 1955 and it was formally initiated at the Belgrade of 1961
It was started at the Belgrade in 1961 with 120 members
It was the group of the non-communist states
explanation: The Non-Aligned Movement was the largest of the three groups at the Bandung Conference of 1955 and it was formally initiated at the first summit of the heads of state at Belgrade in September 1961.

q: The SAARC was founded in 1985 with the charter signed:
explanation: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation was founded with the charter signed in Dhaka on 8 December 1985 and it has its Secretariat in Kathmandu.

q: The modern Commonwealth was:
options: created by the London Declaration of 1949
created by the Balfour Declaration of 1919
created by the 1931 Statute of Westminster
explanation: The modern Commonwealth was created by the London Declaration of 1949 and it is a voluntary association of the sovereign states with the British monarch as the head.

q: The 'Article 367' of the Constitution:
options: Defines the terms of the Government of India and the State
explanation: Article 367 defines the expressions of the Government of India and the State and the Supreme Court and the High Courts and it was amended by the 24th Amendment to remove the Government of India Act of 1935 as the source.

q: The Constitution of India came:
options: the second longest after the USA
into force on 26 January 1950 and it is the longest written constitution
explanation: The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution in the world and it came into force on 26 January 1950, and the original text had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
